record.original_question: Let Delta be a balanced simplicial (d-1)-sphere on vertex set [n], meaning there is a coloring c:[n]->[d] with c(u) != c(v) on every edge. Let Theta = theta_1, ..., theta_d be the colored linear system of parameters defined by theta_i = sum_{c(v)=i} x_v. Does the Artinian reduction S/(I_Delta + (Theta)) always have the strong Lefschetz property, or at least the weak Lefschetz property?

evidence.quote: Problem 4.2. Let ∆ be a balanced simplicial (d − 1)-sphere and Θ = θ1, . . . , θd be a colored linear system of parameters of ∆. Does the algebra S/(I∆ + (Θ)) have the SLP (or WLP)?

A simplicial complex on [n] of dimension (d − 1) is said to be (completely) balanced if there exists a function c : [n] → [d] such that c(v) ≠ c(u) for all edges {u, v} ∈ ∆. ... If ∆ is balanced, then it is known that the sequence of linear forms θ1, . . . , θd defined by θi = Σ_{c(v)=i} xv forms a linear system of parameters of ∆, called a colored linear system of parameters of ∆.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Delta$ be a balanced simplicial $(d-1)$-sphere on vertex set $[n]=\{1,2,\dots,n\}$. Here "balanced" means there exists a coloring $c\colon [n]\to [d]$ such that $c(u)\neq c(v)$ whenever $\{u,v\}$ is an edge of $\Delta$. Let $S=\mathbb{K}[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ be a polynomial ring over a field $\mathbb{K}$ of characteristic $0$, graded by $\deg(x_i)=1$, and let $I_\Delta\subset S$ be the Stanley–Reisner ideal of $\Delta$ (generated by the squarefree monomials $\prod_{v\in F} x_v$ for $F\notin\Delta$). Define the colored linear system of parameters $\Theta=(\theta_1,\dots,\theta_d)$ by
$$\theta_i \;=\; \sum_{v\in [n]:\, c(v)=i} x_v, \qquad i=1,\dots,d.$$
It is known that $\theta_1,\dots,\theta_d$ form a linear system of parameters for the Stanley–Reisner ring $S/I_\Delta$, so the quotient
$$A(\Delta,\Theta) \;=\; S/(I_\Delta + (\theta_1,\dots,\theta_d))$$
is an Artinian standard graded $\mathbb{K}$-algebra with socle in top degree $d$. Recall:
- $A(\Delta,\Theta)$ has the weak Lefschetz property (WLP) if there is a linear form $\ell\in A_1$ such that the multiplication map $\cdot \ell\colon A_i\to A_{i+1}$ has full rank for every $i\geq 0$.
- $A(\Delta,\Theta)$ has the strong Lefschetz property (SLP) if there is a linear form $\ell\in A_1$ such that $\cdot \ell^{j}\colon A_i\to A_{i+j}$ has full rank for all $i,j\geq 0$.

Question: Does $A(\Delta,\Theta)=S/(I_\Delta+(\Theta))$ always have the strong Lefschetz property? At minimum, does it always have the weak Lefschetz property?
artifact.status_search_result: The question appears to be open in full generality. Partial progress exists: the strong Lefschetz property is known for balanced simplicial 3-polytopes (in characteristics other than 2 and 3), and a multigraded strong Lefschetz property has been established for a-balanced homology spheres in characteristic 2. No source found settles SLP or even WLP for arbitrary balanced simplicial spheres with the colored linear system of parameters.

status_evidence.title: Lefschetz properties of balanced 3-polytopes
status_evidence.snippet: The Artinian reduction of the Stanley-Reisner ring of a balanced simplicial 3-polytope with respect to special systems of parameters has the strong Lefschetz property if the characteristic of the base field is not two or three.
status_evidence.claim: SLP is established for balanced simplicial 3-polytopes under characteristic restrictions, indicating only partial progress.

status_evidence.title: Multigraded strong Lefschetz property for balanced simplicial complexes
status_evidence.snippet: The generic N^m-graded Artinian reduction of the Stanley-Reisner ring of an a-balanced homology sphere satisfies the multigraded strong Lefschetz property over a field of characteristic 2.
status_evidence.claim: A multigraded variant of SLP is proved (characteristic 2), not the standard SLP/WLP for the colored l.s.o.p. in general.

status_evidence.title: Weak Lefschetz property of PL-spheres
status_evidence.claim: WLP for general (not necessarily balanced) spheres remains an active research topic, with the balanced case still being investigated.
